confirmed that the majority-negative direction is significantly non-random (p = 0.011),
indicating a weak but consistent community-scale BQH signal.
heading: Finding 1 — Black Queen dynamics are detectable at community scale

text: The 175 NMDC metabolomics samples derive from multiple studies, but 95% of H1 samples (125/131) originate from nmdc:sty-11-r2h77870, making cross-study LC-MS protocol heterogeneity largely absent as a confounder for leucine and arginine.
quote:
The 175 metabolomics samples derive from
  multiple NMDC studies. However, study-level analysis of the H1 subset reveals that
  95% of H1 samples (125/131) originate from a single NMDC study
  (nmdc:sty-11-r2h77870), so cross-study LC-MS protocol heterogeneity is largely
  absent as a confounder for leu and arg.

text: The second NMDC study (n = 6) does not materially affect the H1 results.
quote:
The second study (n = 6) does not
  materially affect the results.
heading: Limitations

text: The report suggests modelling study-level random effects to improve power in future analyses with broader multi-study coverage.

For future analyses with broader multi-study coverage,
  study-level random effects could be modelled to improve power.
heading: Limitations

text: All 33 Freshwater samples lacked paired NMDC metabolomics, making H1 effectively soil-only and leaving freshwater community-scale Black Queen dynamics untested.
quote:
All 33 Freshwater samples lacked paired
  metabolomics in NMDC, so H1 is effectively a soil-only test. Whether BQH dynamics
  operate in freshwater communities at the same scale is untested.
heading: Limitations

text: Abiotic features were all NaN in the 174-sample analysis matrix, preventing partial correlations controlling environmental gradients that could confound H1 and H2.
quote:
Abiotic features (pH, temperature, total organic carbon,
  etc.) were absent (all NaN) for the 174-sample analysis matrix, preventing partial
  correlation tests controlling for environmental gradients. These variables could
  confound both H1 and H2 results.
heading: Limitations

text: GapMind pathway completeness measures gene presence rather than active expression; transcriptomics would be needed to determine whether expressed biosynthesis correlates more strongly with metabolite pools.
quote:
Pathway completeness
  indicates whether the genes are present, not whether they are actively expressed.
  Transcriptomic data would be needed to determine whether expressed biosynthesis
  correlates more strongly with metabolite pools.
heading: Limitations

text: The report matched NMDC metabolites to pathways using string-based compound names.
quote:
Metabolite-to-pathway matching relied on string-based
  compound name matching.
heading: Limitations

text: Automated review identified isoleucine compounds erroneously matching the leucine substring; this was corrected using first-match-wins in NB04 cell-14, and reported results reflect the corrected run.
quote:
A substring collision bug (isoleucine compounds matching the
  "leucine" pattern) was identified by automated review and corrected in NB04 cell-14
  using first-match-wins; results reflect the corrected run.
heading: Limitations

text: Isoleucine is included as a 13th testable pathway but shows a nonsignificant correlation (r = −0.057).

text: The chorismate BQH correlation (r = −0.038) warrants caution because its upstream intermediate proxies reflect precursor availability rather than chorismate pool size.

These are *upstream*
  intermediates, not chorismate itself; their ambient concentrations reflect precursor
